summary: Read all eight Kotlin/GLSL bodies plus graph and launch order. Existing generated push bindings and barriers are deliberate. Add the even-size contract and distinguish buffer rebuilds from live controls; retain the three already-approved helper follow-ups.

lenses.smells_idioms: Typed shared sg* properties and named renderer modules fit the graph. Default buffers are allocated and initialised once per update-box execution, not each GPU frame. Rebuilding update changes buffer identities; measure uses a fixed dispatch group count but a supplier for sgL, so a lattice size change requires measure rebuild too.
lenses.imports: Deterministic rows for Kotlin body hashes 24d7857f and 3261ab88 remove computeMemoryBarrier/computeTask imports as redundant; renderer Options stays. Coordinator applies mechanical imports. No star imports are present.
lenses.whitespace: Kotlin setup, published settings, random state, tick, ordered half-sweeps and bindings form clear groups. Keep GLSL neighbor/bond rows together; long bond-write expressions can wrap within their loop without extracting the documented compiler-sensitive local function.
lenses.comments: Bond directions, double-count avoidance, tick ordering, stats setup ordering and aspect correction are useful. State explicitly that periodic checkerboard updates require positive even L; distinguish mutable runtime controls from the lattice/bond rebuild controls and the dependent-box rerun order.
lenses.glsl: Both compute shaders and vertex/fragment shaders fully read. uint invocation guard matches dispatch rounding; update uses modulo-periodic neighbors and red-black parity, which is safe only for even L. Measure counts right/down bonds once. Vertex emits an oversized triangle; fragment maps UV to an aspect-correct square then flips y for lattice indexing. Keep buffer-reference blocks and pc instance names.
lenses.live_coding: No authored fragment markers or declaration/reset pairs. sgField, sgMode and sgAnneal are supplier-read live values; sgTemperature is overwritten by the tick while annealing is enabled. sgModel is copied to model during buffer creation, so it is a rebuild setting. L changes also require refreshing the cached measure dispatch.
lenses.helpers: computeBarrier(), fullscreenTriangle(), bindPush(m1,m2) and uint Int-lambda support are already approved follow-ups from this example; no new helper requested. The current source has computeTask/computeMemoryBarrier and generated push properties, while no corresponding convenience helper declarations were found. Keep explicit groups=(N+63)/64: automatic local-size dispatch was declined.

findings.issue: The exposed lattice-size edit has an unstated even-size constraint: modulo wrapping on odd L connects same-color checkerboard sites. Also measure caches groups from sgL on its own run while reading current sgL in the push supplier, so changing L in update alone leaves an old dispatch count.
findings.proposed_change: Document positive even L at this setup control, validate it before GPU allocation, and state that size changes rebuild update then measure (then view as the demonstrated run order). Keep manual dispatch group arithmetic.
findings.verification: Replay at two even sizes across a workgroup boundary, rerun the dependent boxes and verify the stats card sees L*L sites. Confirm odd/zero sizes fail before buffer allocation instead of running red-black updates.

findings.issue: Model is read once when bonds are generated, while mode/field/annealing are read each frame. The nearby prop list presents them similarly, making it easy to expect changing sgModel alone to redraw bonds or a manual temperature change to survive enabled annealing.
findings.proposed_change: Briefly mark model/lattice as rebuild controls, and show the runtime gesture sgAnneal=false before changing sgTemperature. State that editing sgModel requires rerunning the bond-initialisation setup; full rerun resets published defaults. Preserve current declarations and no new fragments.
findings.verification: In a real native run change field/mode live, disable annealing and set temperature, then rebuild Gaussian bonds and confirm the distinction through the actual lattice and energy probe.

lenses.smells_idioms: aiTool registers by name and its registry owns rerun/retirement. poolOwner is a stable provider capture used for read-only checks and provenance; keep this intentional capture but initialise with thisBox rather than Box.context.get()!!. getPropertyRaw("code") is justified here: the hash must cover this exact provider sidecar, not an inherited teaching parameter. ToolPool.publish uses that same direct-source contract.
lenses.imports: Deterministic c4a88f81 result keeps completion/diagnostics/models stars and external Jackson/Java imports, removes BoxStudies, and flags token preservation for review. Do not remove uncertain stars by inspection or treat formatter output as an approved semantic patch. Coordinator owns mechanical import changes.
lenses.whitespace: Eight aiTool declarations are useful sections, but semicolon-packed parameter declarations and single-line test/publish actions obscure the argument binding, source guard and mutation boundaries. Expand these steps; break the two large card string concatenations into named note/call content. Retain authored schemas and wording.
lenses.comments: Tool descriptions usefully distinguish listing, reading, explicit testing, local curation and notes from certification. Add one brief comment that poolOwner captures the registering provider for later action callbacks, and one around the atomic note write and exact version/source identity. Avoid comments repeating each check.
lenses.glsl: No GLSL or embedded shader code; HTML output has a dark background, Iosevka font and escaping for external text.
lenses.live_coding: No fragment markers or declaration/reset pairs. Rerunning is a provider registration refresh; button redraw reads current registry and persisted versions. Keep callback owner stable and verify old registration removal rather than adding a manual teardown/once wrapper.
lenses.helpers: Existing aiTool and ToolPool already own registration and immutable provider versioning. New candidate: typed durable version-note read/append on ToolPool, so provider boxes do not recreate its filesystem layout, source validation, JSON casts and atomic persistence. No matching note API in ToolPool.kt; no declined proposal overlaps.

summary: Read the full study UI and actual KratosStudy/Session/frames/output APIs. Preserve one worker and explicit frame polling, but verify callback cancellation uses a real throw, move the winner field solve off the frame coroutine, finish progress per action, and correct the target-change cache claim.

lenses.smells_idioms: No raw properties or box aliases. Atomic control snapshots are appropriate for background solver work. Session finally closes the current worker, and thenAccept closes a late opening. However the sample callback uses unqualified error in box scope (Box.error displays Unit), and winner resultAt calls blocking Future.get inside frames. Detached supplyAsync also needs the per-run cancel flag set during shutdown so the next callback aborts instead of continuing after session close.
lenses.imports: Deterministic cf25b48c result keeps kratos star, ManifoldLibrary and Java concurrent imports; marks frames/markdown/mdEscape/mesh imports redundant. It is a preservation-review candidate, not an approved patch; coordinator must inspect its token changes and compile before adopting formatting. No speculative star removal.
lenses.whitespace: Controls, startup, commands, future completion and result presentation already have useful groups; wrap named slider/MeshView args and repeated formatted units for scanning. Dense n*n/2 arithmetic and one-line status update can receive mechanical spacing without hiding the grid/search budgets.
lenses.comments: Physical units, conduction model, optional setup and cache reuse at fixed target are useful. The claim that changing target throws away nothing reusable is false for the current API: KratosStudyDemo.study creates a new KratosStudy whose scalar cache is instance-local. Cancellation comments require an actual throw, not Box.error.
lenses.glsl: No GLSL or shader strings. Figures/mesh renders are produced by simulation APIs; preserve real solver-based landscape and field output, with no substituted capture.
lenses.live_coding: No authored fragment markers or declaration/reset pairs. Controls supply target and grid size while one frames coroutine polls completion. Whole-box rerun must cancel the active study and close its worker without presenting old results; retain the late-opening close path. Do not block the frame coroutine on the extra winner solve.
lenses.helpers: Already uses markdown/mdEscape, controlGroup, progressReporter and showMeshGrid. Existing withProgress illustrates operation lifetime but does not justify wrapping this entire persistent frames loop; finish each reporter at action completion. Numeric template .fN shortcuts are already approved, so their reuse is an approved follow-up, not a new proposal.

findings.issue: The callback intends to throw to abort grid/optimise, but box code has Box.error via HasOutput, which returns Unit and displays an error. BoxAiTools.kt explicitly documents this shadowing. The same call occurs at line 112; if resolved to the member, Cancel continues solving and repeatedly reports an error instead of aborting.
findings.proposed_change: Use an explicit thrown exception or qualified kotlin.error at both callback sites. Signal cancelling in the frames finally path before closing the worker so an old background loop aborts on its next callback. Preserve cached completed samples and distinguish Cancel from solver failure.
findings.verification: Compile in the actual box receiver context, launch a real bounded grid and search, press Cancel during a solve and verify no next solve is submitted after its callback. Confirm the expected Cancelled message, retained cached samples, and Stop/rerun cleanup during opening and active work.

findings.issue: After the asynchronous sweep completes, this call runs inside frames. KratosStudy.resultAt submits an additional solve then blocks with future.get(timeoutSeconds,...), so the frame coroutine can stall the Runloop while waiting for the winning field; Cancel/Stop feedback can become unresponsive at the end of the operation.
findings.proposed_change: Include winner-field recovery in the background operation using the same captured active study and target, or return a separate future and poll it with frame(). Publish geometry/status only for the current run after the future completes.
findings.verification: Use the real Kratos worker and verify Runloop/UI controls remain responsive during the winner re-solve as well as the sweep; cancel or rerun at that point and confirm no old result is published and the worker closes.

findings.snippet: solves are the same solves, so nothing is thrown away that could be reused.
findings.issue: Target changes call KratosStudyDemo.study again, constructing a fresh instance whose private cache starts empty. Only the background domain/worker survives; scalar samples from the previous target study are not reused by this code.
findings.proposed_change: State that changing the target keeps the worker/background grid but starts a fresh study cache. Treat any cross-target reuse API as a separate design decision rather than asserting it already happens.
findings.verification: Read current study constructor and cache ownership; in a later actual run repeat a grid at one target to see cache hits, then change target and confirm the new study solve count/cache behavior matches the revised comment.

findings.issue: A cancelled or failed operation may stop below expected and leave its progress bar active for the remainder of the persistent frames loop. progress.finish() runs only when the whole box exits, and the next command overwrites the reporter reference.
findings.proposed_change: Finish and clear the per-operation reporter in the completion handling finally path for success, cancellation and failure. Keep the outer finally as a final shutdown safeguard.
findings.verification: Cancel a partially completed real grid, induce a specific solver failure, and then launch another grid/search. Confirm the previous reporter is removed and the new operation has one current progress bar.
